Package com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.infrastructure.web.conversation

Class ConversationsController

java.lang.Object
com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.infrastructure.web.conversation.ConversationsController
@RestController public class ConversationsController extends Object
REST adapter for the /conversations endpoints (design §6.2.8).

The /api/v1 prefix is applied centrally by WebConfig; no class-level @RequestMapping.

Class-level @PreAuthorize is not needed — the URL guard /api/v1/conversations/** → hasAnyRole("STANDARD", "ADMIN", "SYSTEM") in SpringSecurityConfig admits exactly the three principal kinds that may reach this surface (design §8.6). The AuthenticationPrincipal is the sealed Principal, and ConversationOwner.from(Principal) dispatches exhaustively to the matching ConversationOwner variant — owner-scoping for each specific conversation is enforced inside the per-endpoint service.

    • sendMessage

      @PostMapping(value="/conversations/{conversationId}/messages", produces="text/event-stream", consumes="application/json") public org.springframework.web.servlet.mvc.method.annotation.SseEmitter sendMessage(@AuthenticationPrincipal Principal principal, @PathVariable("conversationId") UUID conversationId, @Valid @RequestBody @Valid SendMessageRequest request, jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest httpRequest)
      Streamed chat turn (design §7, §16.2). Returns a SseEmitter bound to a cold Flux of TurnEvents. The synchronous prefix of SendMessageUseCase.send(com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.application.chat.SendMessageUseCase.SendMessageCommand) runs in this method body — cap / cross-owner / 404 / 400 failures throw before the emitter is created and the global handler writes the matching JSON Problem-Details body (HTTP 4xx/5xx, content type application/problem+json; the SSE stream is never opened).

      Reactive errors signaled by the use case AFTER the started frame are translated by SseErrorTranslator into an error SSE frame on the open stream; the HTTP status stays 200 (headers already flushed). Client disconnect / timeout disposes the subscription via the Reactor Disposable → cancellation propagates through the OpenAI adapter's reactive HTTP client and releases the upstream connection (US-11-006 / REQ-STR-003).
